data.scenario_text: From the top of a lighthouse <m>140</m> feet above sea level, the angle of depression of a boat out at sea is <m>31^\circ</m>.
data.find_task: Find the straight-line distance from the top of the lighthouse to the boat. Do not round until the final answer; then round to two decimal places as necessary.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). A correct sketch shows a right triangle with the right angle marked, the given 31^\circ angle placed at the correct vertex, and the one given length written on its correct side: the leg opposite the given angle is 140\text{ ft}. The other two side lengths are not given, so they stay unlabeled. The 31^\circ angle belongs at the boat, not at the top of the lighthouse: the angle of depression stated at the top and the angle of elevation at the boat are alternate interior angles, with the horizontal through the top of the lighthouse parallel to the sea.

Part (b). The angle of depression is measured downward from a horizontal line through the top of the lighthouse. Because that line is parallel to the surface of the sea, alternate interior angles give a congruent angle of elevation at the boat, so the 31^\circ angle is the one inside the triangle at the boat.

Read the triangle from that angle: the straight-line distance from the top of the lighthouse to the boat is the hypotenuse, and the known quantity is the leg opposite the given angle. The one basic ratio that uses exactly those two sides is sine, \sin\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}, so that is the ratio to use.

Substituting and computing, L=\frac{140}{\sin(31^\circ)}.

So the straight-line distance from the top of the lighthouse to the boat is \boxed{271.82\text{ ft}}.
